White has just played c4, putting direct pressure on my d5 pawn. Right now d5 is only defended by the queen, so I should either support the center or resolve the tension. Moving c6 reinforces d5 with a pawn, keeps the position solid, and preserves the option to develop the c8 bishop actively. It also prepares natural moves like Nf6 and e6 without creating weaknesses.

Tactically, there is no immediate threat against my position after c6, and White will need to develop before fighting for the center. This keeps the balance while avoiding the pawn loss from d5 being captured.

Move: c6

The position is a Slav Defense with central tension between White's c4-pawn and Black's d5-pawn. Black’s setup with ...c6 is solid, preparing to recapture on d5 if White exchanges. White’s main goal is to develop naturally while keeping central options open.

**Nf3** is the most flexible and principled move: it develops a piece, controls the important e5 square, supports the d4-pawn, and keeps the central tension. White can follow up with Nc3, e3, or Bf4 depending on Black's response. There is no immediate tactical rush, so improving the position is best.

Move: Nf3

Black should develop and keep the central tension. The move **Nf6** brings another piece into play, adds a defender to d5, and discourages White from playing e4 too quickly. It also keeps flexible options like ...e6 or ...Bf5 next, while avoiding the early complications of taking on c4 before developing.

Move: Nf6

White is still in the opening fight for the center. Black’s last move ...Nf6 reinforces d5 and prepares to develop, while also eyeing e4. White should develop to keep the central tension alive. Nc3 is the natural move, bringing another piece into play, supporting d4 and preparing the important e2-e4 pawn break later. If Black tries ...dxc4, White can continue with a4 or recapture comfortably.

Move: Nc3

Black can capture the white c-pawn and go into the main Slav Accepted structure. The pawn on d5 is currently under pressure, so taking on c4 relieves the tension, wins a pawn, and sets up the typical plan of supporting the extra pawn with ...b5 followed by ...Bf5. There is no immediate tactic that allows White to regain the pawn cheaply.

Move: dxc4
